title: Your Anxiety Isn't a Warning — It's a Forecast Your Brain Already Believes
description:
3 a.m. Nothing in the room is moving. The door is locked. And your heart is already running. Your body isn't reacting to danger — it's rehearsing it. And it's been rehearsing all day.

This video reframes anxiety as a threat forecast: a prediction the nervous system casts before conscious thought, fed by an intolerance of uncertainty and written into the body before the mind finds a reason. Once you see anxiety as a forecast rather than evidence, the whole experience changes shape.

Referenced: LeDoux, The Emotional Brain (1996) · LeDoux & Pine (2016) · Grupe & Nitschke (2013) · Carleton, intolerance of uncertainty (2016).

Autopilot makes calm, research-grounded explainers about the predictive brain — why you think, feel, and act the way you do. No hype, no quick fixes. Just the mechanism.

This video is for education only and is not medical advice. If anxiety is overwhelming you, please reach out to a qualified professional.
